Now evaluate each benefit.

1. Pension Credit (Guarantee Credit) - rules PC-1 to PC-5.

PC-1: Claimant must live in England, Scotland, or Wales and have reached State Pension age.
- F3: Wales, F17: age 74 > 66. So condition met.

PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age (simplified). F4 and F16: has_partner = no. So no partner condition needed.

PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income.
- Savings = £52,419. Excess over £10,000 = £42,419. Every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. Number of £500 units: ceil(42419/500) = ceil(84.838) = 85. So deemed income from savings = £85 per week.

PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold.
- Assessed weekly income = actual weekly income + deemed income from savings.
- Actual weekly income = £418.04 (F6). Deemed income = £85. Total assessed income = £503.04.
- Threshold for single = £238. Assessed income (£503.04) > £238, so not eligible.

PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between the threshold and assessed weekly income. Since assessed income > threshold, difference negative, so not eligible.

Thus pension_credit: not_eligible.

But need to check if any other income? Only weekly_income_total given. Savings deemed income calculated. So decision: not_eligible.

2. Attendance Allowance - rules AA-1 to AA-7.

AA-1: Must have reached State Pension age. Yes (F17, F18).
AA-2: Must have a physical or mental disability or health condition severe enough to need help with personal care or supervision.
- F15: needs_care_help = no. So condition not met.
AA-3: Must have needed that help for at least 6 months. Not applicable since needs_care_help = no.
AA-4: Must have been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years. F5: yes.
AA-5: Cannot get AA if already receiving DLA, PIP, or ADP. F9: receives_dla_or_pip = no.
AA-6: Rates.
AA-7: Scheme covers England and Wales; people in Scotland apply for Pension Age Disability Payment. F3: Wales, so covered.

Since needs_care_help = no, he does not meet the disability requirement. So not_eligible.

3. Council Tax Reduction (pensioners) - rules CTR-1 to CTR-6.

CTR-1: Available to people on low income or claiming benefits, up to 100% reduction. Each council runs its own scheme; model covers pensioners in England and Wales.
CTR-2: Pensioner scheme applies to people who have reached State Pension age. Yes (F17, F18).
CTR-3: Applicant must be liable to pay council tax on the home they live in. F12: council_tax_liable = yes.
CTR-4: People who get Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get maximum reduction (100%). F7: receives_pension_credit = no.
CTR-5: Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction.
- Capital = savings = £52,419 > £16,000. So cannot get reduction.
CTR-6: Otherwise, weekly reduction calculation... but CTR-5 says capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. So not eligible.

Thus council_tax_reduction: not_eligible.

Reason: Capital (savings £52,419) exceeds the £16,000 limit for Council Tax Reduction for pensioners not on Guarantee Credit.

4. Warm Home Discount - rules WHD-1 to WHD-4.

WHD-1: Scheme covers England and Wales only. F3: Wales, so covered.
WHD-2: On 23 August 2026, claimant or partner must have been receiving a qualifying means-tested benefit: Pension Credit, Housing Benefit, Universal Credit, or income-related ESA.
- F10: receives_qualifying_benefit_on_whd_date = no. So condition not met.
WHD-3: On 23 August 2026, claimant's or partner's name must have been on the electricity bill. Missing info: electricity_bill_in_name not provided.
WHD-4: Discount is one-off £150.

Since WHD-2 fails (no qualifying benefit), not eligible regardless of electricity bill. So not_eligible.

Reason: The claimant was not receiving a qualifying means-tested benefit on 23 August 2026.
